editorial:
Imagine meeting a guy who believes he is the greatest musician on the planet, but the catch is that he actually cannot sing a single note. That is exactly who you get with John of God. You follow an American filmmaker who travels all the way to Kinshasa in the DR Congo to make a documentary about this legendary character. The vibe is light, funny, and full of energy. You get to see the contrast between John's massive ego and his actual lack of skill, which makes for some really hilarious moments as he tries to convince everyone of his greatness.

What really works here is the acting and the colorful setting of Congo. The pacing stays quick, so you never feel bored, though some of the comedy is a bit silly. It is a great pick if you love stories about delusional characters who are somehow lovable.
endingExplained: In the end, John's delusions are finally put to the test during a big performance. While he still thinks he is a superstar, the world sees the truth about his singing. However, the movie wraps up by showing that his confidence and charm are what actually make him special, not his voice. He doesn't really change who he is, but he finds a way to be happy with his fame regardless of the noise he makes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mockumentaries and underdog stories.
